picks.title: Giving AI a 'crystal clear' view of the materials world
picks.excerpt: MIT researchers built an AI model that pairs 3D atomic structures with natural-language descriptions from papers and databases to identify optimal crystalline materials for target applications.
picks.rationale: Materials slot and the freshest item from a top outlet: a model that ties 3D crystal structures to text from the literature so it can rank materials for a given application.

picks.title: Riverlane and NVIDIA use AI to speed up quantum decoder calibration
picks.excerpt: Riverlane and NVIDIA are testing AI and GPU acceleration to speed up quantum error-correction decoder calibration as quantum hardware behaviour drifts.
picks.rationale: Quantum slot: AI recalibrates error-correction decoders as the hardware drifts. This is a different project from the 10-18 Claude circuit card and the 9-27 Meridian card.

picks.title: Switching languages can change a chatbot's personality test results
picks.excerpt: USTC researchers gave five chatbots Big Five personality questionnaires in English and Mandarin (one also in French); answers held steady within a language but trait scores shifted in model-specific directions when the language changed.
picks.rationale: Psychology slot and the newest item in the pool: Big Five scores for five chatbots stay stable within one language but shift when the language changes, which matters for anyone using LLMs in survey or psychometric research.

picks.title: Forecasting air drag with deep learning helps predict when uncontrolled satellites and rocket stages fall to Earth
picks.excerpt: A hybrid of Newtonian orbital mechanics and a neural network that learns how an object's ballistic coefficient changes over time, trained on 11 years of tracking data, kept reentry predictions within their uncertainty windows.
picks.rationale: Space-physics slot: a model that pairs orbital mechanics with a neural network, trained on 11 years of tracking data, keeps reentry forecasts for debris inside their uncertainty windows.

picks.title: Astronomers want your help finding 'missing' black holes in the Milky Way
picks.excerpt: A citizen-science project asks volunteers to comb NASA telescope data for hidden black holes, because AI classifiers struggle with stellar flares and pulsations in the light curves.
picks.rationale: Astronomy slot: a new citizen-science project launched because AI classifiers miss black-hole signals hidden among stellar flares and pulsations. It shows where people still beat the model.
